title: Update vulnerable dependencies under strict warnings
goal: Apply vulnerability-driven package updates without permanently weakening warnings-as-errors, then restore and test the resulting dependency graph.

selectionNotes: Preview-restore audit handling is not global warning suppression; unrelated restore errors still prevent updates.
Controlled advisory metadata demonstrates command behavior, not the security of a real dependency or every transitive remediation.

runtime.name: .NET
runtime.reason: Runtime of the selected SDK build/package tooling; this route is catalogued for target 11.

sdk.name: .NET SDK
sdk.reason: The documented .NET 11 SDK/MSBuild/NuGet command behavior; exact RC2 verification is recorded separately.

language.name: C#
language.reason: Language mode of the canonical compiled verification consumer. Served XML and CLI configuration is language-neutral and requires no application language migration.

platforms: Platforms supported by the .NET SDK; actual authoring checks ran on Windows x64. No Framework MSBuild.exe or native OS execution evidence.
prerequisites: Inspect effective global.json, project imports, shared build files and NuGet configuration before applying the migration.
Use an existing authorized package source for package commands; replace the example.invalid URL. Publication metadata and audit data are source capabilities, not credentials supplied by Playbook.
constraints: Preview-restore audit handling is not global warning suppression; unrelated restore errors still prevent updates.
Controlled advisory metadata demonstrates command behavior, not the security of a real dependency or every transitive remediation.
Target 11 only. .NET 10 is a verified comparison, not an added foundation or a declared older-target route.
Consulting Playbook serves embedded documentation only; no consumer build, package update, account or resource is created.
stabilityLimitations: Verified using SDK 11.0.100-rc.2.26504.105, not GA. No publisher-designated experimental API is used; GA reconciliation remains separate.

evidence.scope: Actual compilation and execution of the original SDK behavior checks on Windows x64. Package tests use controlled loopback V3 metadata and synthetic advisories with real NuGet commands, not a production feed/security validation. Build tests verify XML outputs and wave diagnostics, not all historical wave internals.
